translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Prince of Rencheng Hui was made Right Chancellor; Grand Preceptor Prince of Fenyang Run was made Grand Commandant; Prince of Lanling Chang Gong was made Grand Marshal; Prince of Guangning Xiaoxing was made Grand General; and Prince of Ande Tingzong was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Prince of Rencheng Hui was made Right Chancellor, Grand Preceptor Prince of Fenyang Run Grand Commandant, Prince of Lanling Chang Gong Grand Marshal, Prince of Guangning Xiaoxing Grand General, and Prince of Ande Tingzong Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 使領軍封輔相聘於周。

translations.literal: General of the Guard Feng Fuxiang was sent on a diplomatic mission to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guard Feng Fuxiang was sent to Zhou as envoy.

sentences.zh: 戊子，拜右昭儀胡氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, Honored Consort Hu was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Honored Consort Hu was made empress.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以司州牧、北平王仁堅為尚書令，特進許季良為左僕射，彭城王寶德為右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, Governor of Si Province Prince of Beiping Renjian was made Minister of Works; Special Advance Xu Jiliang was made Left Vice Minister; and Prince of Pengcheng Baode was made Right Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Governor of Si Province Prince of Beiping Renjian was made Minister of Works, Special Advance Xu Jiliang Left Vice Minister, and Prince of Pengcheng Baode Right Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，行幸晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, the Emperor traveled to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 是月，《聖壽堂御覽》成，敕付史閣。

translations.literal: That month the Shengshou Hall Imperial Digest was completed and ordered deposited in the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Shengshou Hall Imperial Digest was finished and sent to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 後改為《修文殿御覽》。

translations.literal: Later it was renamed the Xiucheng Hall Imperial Digest.
translations.idiomatic: It was later renamed the Xiucheng Hall Imperial Digest.

sentences.zh: 九月，陳人來聘。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, people from Chen came on a diplomatic visit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month envoys arrived from Chen.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，降死罪已下囚。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, prisoners down to those guilty of capital crimes were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, tenth month, prisoners below capital offense were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 甲午，拜弘德夫人穆氏為左皇后，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, Honored Lady Mu was installed as Left Empress, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Honored Lady Mu was made Left Empress and a general pardon was declared.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛丑，廢皇后胡氏為庶人。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou of the twelfth month, Empress Hu was deposed and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou in the twelfth month, Empress Hu was deposed and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 是歲，新羅、百濟、勿吉、突厥並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That year, Silla, Baekje, Wuji, and the Turks all sent envoys to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year tribute came from Silla, Baekje, Wuji, and the Turks.

sentences.zh: 於周為建德元年。

translations.literal: In Zhou this was the first year of Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou it was Jiande year one.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月戊寅，以並省尚書令高阿那肱為錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the fourth year, on the day wuyin, Minister of Works of the Combined Provinces Gao Anagou was put in charge of recording affairs in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year four, first month, on wuyin, Minister of Works of the Combined Provinces Gao Anagou was made Recorder of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔兼散騎常侍崔象使於陳。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, an edict ordered concurrent Supervising Cavalier Attendant Cui Xiang to go as envoy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the court ordered concurrent Supervising Cavalier Attendant Cui Xiang to Chen.

sentences.zh: 是月，鄴都、并州並有狐媚，多截人發。

translations.literal: That month, fox-spirits appeared in both Ye and Bing Province and cut off many people's hair.
translations.idiomatic: That month fox-demons appeared at Ye and Bing Province and cut off many people's hair.

sentences.zh: 二月乙巳，拜左皇后穆氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On the day yisi of the second month, Left Empress Lady Mu was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi in the second month, Left Empress Lady Mu was made empress.

sentences.zh: 丙午，置文林館。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, the Wenlin Hall was established.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the Wenlin Hall was established.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以尚書令、北平王仁堅為錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, Minister of Works Prince of Beiping Renjian was put in charge of recording affairs in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Minister of Works Prince of Beiping Renjian was made Recorder of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，行幸晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi, the Emperor traveled to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi the emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 是月，周人來聘。

translations.literal: That month, people from Zhou came on a diplomatic visit.
translations.idiomatic: That month envoys arrived from Zhou.

sentences.zh: 三月辛未，盜入信州，殺刺史和士休，南兗州刺史鮮于世榮討之。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei of the third month, bandits entered Xin Province and killed Governor He Shixiu; Governor of Southern Yan Province Xianyu Shirong campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the third month, bandits entered Xin Province and killed Governor He Shixiu; Governor of Southern Yan Province Xianyu Shirong marched against them.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，車駕至晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, the imperial carriage reached Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the emperor arrived at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊午，以大司馬、蘭陵王長恭為太保，大將軍、定州刺史、南陽王綽為大司馬，大司馬、太尉衛菩薩為大將軍，司徒、安德王延宗為太尉，司空、武興王普為司徒，開府儀同三司、宜陽王趙彥深為司空。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu of the fourth month of summer, Grand Marshal Prince of Lanling Chang Gong was made Grand Preceptor; Grand General, Governor of Ding Province, Prince of Nanyang Chuo was made Grand Marshal; Grand Marshal and Grand Commandant Wei Pusa was made Grand General; Minister over the Masses Prince of Ande Tingzong was made Grand Commandant; Minister of Works Prince of Wuxing Pu was made Minister over the Masses; and Bearer of Equal Honor with the Three Excellencies Prince of Yiyang Zhao Yanshen was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, fourth month, on wuwu, Grand Marshal Prince of Lanling Chang Gong was made Grand Preceptor, Grand General and Governor of Ding Province Prince of Nanyang Chuo Grand Marshal, Grand Marshal and Grand Commandant Wei Pusa Grand General, Minister over the Masses Prince of Ande Tingzong Grand Commandant, Minister of Works Prince of Wuxing Pu Minister over the Masses, and Bearer of Equal Honor with the Three Excellencies Prince of Yiyang Zhao Yanshen Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，祈皇祠。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Shrine.

sentences.zh: 壇壝蕝之內忽有車軌之轍，案驗，傍無人跡，不知車所從來。

translations.literal: Within the altar enclosure and its screens, wheel tracks suddenly appeared; on investigation there were no human footprints nearby, and no one knew whence the carriage had come.
translations.idiomatic: Within the altar enclosure wheel tracks suddenly appeared; no footprints were found nearby, and no one knew where the carriage had come from.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔以為大慶，班告天下。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, an edict proclaimed this a great auspice and announced it throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao an edict declared this a great omen and proclaimed it to the empire.

sentences.zh: 己未，周人來聘。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, people from Zhou came on a diplomatic visit.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei envoys arrived from Zhou.

sentences.zh: 五月丙子，詔史官更撰《魏書》。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi of the fifth month, an edict ordered the historiographers to compile a new History of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingzi, the court ordered the historiographers to compile a new History of Wei.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以領軍穆提婆為尚書左僕射，以侍中、中書監段孝言為右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, General of the Guard Mu Tipo was made Left Vice Minister of Works, and Palace Attendant and Secretariat Supervisor Duan Xiaoyan was made Right Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, General of the Guard Mu Tipo was made Left Vice Minister of Works, and Palace Attendant and Secretariat Supervisor Duan Xiaoyan was made Right Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 是月，開府儀同三司尉破胡、長孫洪略等與陳將吳明徹戰於呂梁南。

translations.literal: That month, Bearer of Equal Honor with the Three Excellencies Wei Pohu, Zhangsun Honglue, and others fought Chen general Wu Mingche south of Lüliang.
translations.idiomatic: That month Bearer of Equal Honor with the Three Excellencies Wei Pohu and Zhangsun Honglue fought Chen general Wu Mingche south of Lüliang.

sentences.zh: 大敗，破胡走以免，洪略戰歿。

translations.literal: They were utterly defeated; Pohu fled and escaped, and Honglue died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: They were routed; Pohu fled and survived, while Honglue fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 遂陷秦、涇二州。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qin and Jing provinces were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Jing provinces then fell.

sentences.zh: 明徹進陷和、合二州。

translations.literal: Mingche advanced and also took He and He provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche went on to take He and He provinces as well.

sentences.zh: 是月，殺太保、蘭陵王長恭。

translations.literal: That month, Grand Preceptor Prince of Lanling Chang Gong was killed.
translations.idiomatic: That month Grand Preceptor Prince of Lanling Chang Gong was put to death.

sentences.zh: 六月，明徹進軍圍壽陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Mingche advanced and besieged Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Mingche marched on and besieged Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 壬子，幸南苑，從官暍死者六十人。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, the Emperor visited the Southern Park; sixty attendants died of heatstroke.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi he visited the Southern Park; sixty attendants died of heatstroke.

sentences.zh: 以錄尚書事高阿那肱為司徒。

translations.literal: Recorder of the Ministry of Works Gao Anagou was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Recorder of the Ministry of Works Gao Anagou was made Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，詔開府王師羅使於周。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, an edict ordered Bearer of the Office Wang Shiluo to go as envoy to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the court ordered Bearer of the Office Wang Shiluo to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，校獵於鄴東。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn, a hunting review was held east of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, ninth month, he held a hunting review east of Ye.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，陳將吳明徹陷壽陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, Chen general Wu Mingche took Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, tenth month, Chen general Wu Mingche captured Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，殺侍中崔季舒、張雕唐、散騎常侍劉逖、封孝琰、黃門侍郎裴澤、郭遵。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Palace Attendants Cui Jishu, Zhang Diaotang, Supervising Cavalier Attendants Liu Ti and Feng Xiaoyan, and Yellow Gate Gentlemen Pei Ze and Guo Zun were killed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Palace Attendants Cui Jishu and Zhang Diaotang, Supervising Cavalier Attendants Liu Ti and Feng Xiaoyan, and Yellow Gate Gentlemen Pei Ze and Guo Zun were put to death.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，行幸晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, the Emperor traveled to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊寅，以司徒高阿那肱為右丞相。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin of the twelfth month, Minister over the Masses Gao Anagou was made Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin in the twelfth month, Minister over the Masses Gao Anagou was made Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 是歲，高麗、靺鞨並遣使朝貢，突厥使求婚。

translations.literal: That year, Goguryeo and Mohe both sent envoys to pay tribute, and the Turks sent envoys seeking marriage.
translations.idiomatic: That year tribute came from Goguryeo and Mohe, and the Turks sent envoys seeking a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月乙丑，置左右娥英各一人。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the fifth year, on the day yichou, one Left and one Right Eying were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year five, first month, on yichou, one Left and one Right Eying were appointed.

sentences.zh: 二月乙未，車駕至自晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei of the second month, the imperial carriage returned from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei in the second month the emperor returned from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 朔州行臺、南安王思好反。

translations.literal: Regional Inspector of Shuo Province Prince of Nan'an Sihao rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Inspector of Shuo Province Prince of Nan'an Sihao rebelled.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，行幸晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, the Emperor traveled to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 尚書令唐邕等大破思好，投火死，焚其屍，並其妻李氏。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Tang Yong and others routed Sihao; he threw himself into the fire and died, his corpse was burned, and his wife Lady Li with it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Tang Yong and others crushed Sihao; he threw himself into the fire and died, and his corpse was burned together with his wife Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 丁未，車駕至自晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, the imperial carriage returned from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the emperor returned from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以尚書令唐邕為錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, Minister of Works Tang Yong was put in charge of recording affairs in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Minister of Works Tang Yong was made Recorder of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，大旱，晉陽得死魃，長二尺，面頂各二目。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer, a great drought struck; at Jinyang a dead drought-demon was found, two feet long, with two eyes each on its face and crown.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, fifth month, drought was severe; at Jinyang a dead drought-demon was found, two feet long, with two eyes on face and crown alike.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，使刻木為其形以獻。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of it, he had a wooden image carved in its likeness and presented.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, the emperor had a wooden image carved in its likeness and presented.

sentences.zh: 庚申，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen a general pardon was declared.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，陳人寇淮北。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, people from Chen raided north of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Chen forces raided north of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 秋八月癸卯，行幸晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day guimao of the eighth month of autumn, the Emperor traveled to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, eighth month, on guimao, the emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以高勱為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, Gao Li was made Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Gao Li was appointed Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 是歲，殺南陽王綽。

translations.literal: That year, Prince of Nanyang Chuo was killed.
translations.idiomatic: That year Prince of Nanyang Chuo was put to death.

sentences.zh: 六年春三月乙亥，車駕至自晉陽。

translations.literal: In the third month of spring of the sixth year, on the day yihai, the imperial carriage returned from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year six, third month, on yihai, the emperor returned from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，烹妖賊鄭子饒於都市。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, the sorcerer-rebel Zheng Zirao was boiled alive in the market.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the sorcerer-rebel Zheng Zirao was boiled alive in the market.

sentences.zh: 是月，周人來聘。

translations.literal: That month, people from Zhou came on a diplomatic visit.
translations.idiomatic: That month envoys arrived from Zhou.

sentences.zh: 夏四月庚子，以中書監陽休之為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi of the fourth month of summer, Secretariat Supervisor Yang Xiuzhi was made Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, fourth month, on gengzi, Secretariat Supervisor Yang Xiuzhi was appointed Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，靺鞨遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, Mohe sent envoys to pay tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao envoys came with tribute from Mohe.

sentences.zh: 秋七月甲戌，行幸晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu of the seventh month of autumn, the Emperor traveled to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, seventh month, on jiaxu, the emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 八月丁酉，冀、定、趙、幽、滄、瀛六州大水。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou of the eighth month, Ji, Ding, Zhao, You, Cang, and Ying provinces suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou in the eighth month, Ji, Ding, Zhao, You, Cang, and Ying provinces were inundated.

sentences.zh: 是月，周師入洛川，屯芒山，攻逼洛城。

translations.literal: That month, Zhou armies entered the Luo River valley, encamped on Mang Mountain, and pressed the attack on Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That month Zhou forces entered the Luo valley, encamped on Mang Mountain, and pressed Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 縱火船焚浮橋，河橋絕。

translations.literal: Fire ships were sent to burn the pontoon bridge, and the river crossing was cut.
translations.idiomatic: Fire ships burned the pontoon bridge and severed the crossing.

sentences.zh: 閏月己丑，遣右丞相高阿那肱自晉陽禦之，師次河陽，周師夜遁。

translations.literal: On the day jichou of the intercalary month, Right Chancellor Gao Anagou was dispatched from Jinyang to meet them; his army halted at Heyang, and the Zhou armies fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou in the intercalary month, Right Chancellor Gao Anagou was sent from Jinyang to meet them; his army halted at Heyang and the Zhou forces fled by night.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以司空趙彥深為司徒，斛律阿列羅為司空。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Minister of Works Zhao Yanshen was made Minister over the Masses, and Hulu Alieluo was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Minister of Works Zhao Yanshen was made Minister over the Masses and Hulu Alieluo was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以軍國資用不足，稅關市、舟車、山澤、鹽鐵、店肆，輕重各有差，開酒禁。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, because state and army funds were insufficient, taxes were levied on markets, boats and carts, mountains and marshes, salt and iron, and shops, each according to degree, and the ban on wine was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, with state funds exhausted, taxes were imposed on markets, transport, mountains, salt, iron, and shops by degree, and the wine ban was lifted.

sentences.zh: 是月，以水澇，遣使巡撫流亡人戶。

translations.literal: That month, because of flood damage, envoys were dispatched to succor displaced households.
translations.idiomatic: That month envoys were sent to succor displaced households after the floods.

sentences.zh: 八月丁卯，行幸晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao of the eighth month, the Emperor traveled to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dingmao, the emperor went to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 雉集於御坐，獲之，有司不敢以聞。

translations.literal: Pheasants gathered on the imperial seat; they were caught, but the relevant offices dared not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Pheasants gathered on the imperial seat; they were caught, but officials dared not report it.

sentences.zh: 詔營邯鄲宮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered construction of the Handan palace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Handan palace built.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙辰，帝大狩於祁連池。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen of the tenth month of winter, the Emperor held a great hunt at Qilian Pool.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, tenth month, on bingchen, the emperor held a great hunt at Qilian Pool.

sentences.zh: 周師攻晉州。

translations.literal: Zhou armies attacked Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou forces attacked Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，帝還晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, the Emperor returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai the emperor returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 甲子，出兵，大集晉祠。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, troops were mobilized and a great assembly held at Jin Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi troops were mobilized and a great muster held at Jin Shrine.

sentences.zh: 庚午，帝發晉陽。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, the Emperor set out from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the emperor marched out from Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，帝列陣而行，上雞棲原，與周齊王憲相對，至夜不戰。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, the Emperor drew up his battle lines and advanced, ascending Jixi Plain and facing Zhou Prince of Qi Xian; they stood opposite until night without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the emperor advanced in battle order, climbed Jixi Plain, and faced Zhou Prince of Qi Xian; neither side fought until night.

sentences.zh: 周師斂陣而退。

translations.literal: The Zhou armies withdrew their formations and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou forces withdrew and retreated.

sentences.zh: 十一月，周武帝退還長安，留偏師守晉州，高阿那肱等圍晉州城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Emperor Wu of Zhou returned to Chang'an, leaving a detached force to hold Jin Province; Gao Anagou and others besieged the city of Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhou Emperor Wu returned to Chang'an, leaving a detachment to hold Jin Province while Gao Anagou and others besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，帝至圍所。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, the Emperor reached the siege camp.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the emperor reached the siege camp.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊申，周武帝來救晉州。

translations.literal: On the day wushen of the twelfth month, Emperor Wu of Zhou came to relieve Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen in the twelfth month Zhou Emperor Wu came to relieve Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，戰於城南，齊軍大敗。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, battle was joined south of the city and the Qi army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu battle was joined south of the city and the Qi army was routed.

sentences.zh: 帝棄軍先還。

translations.literal: The Emperor abandoned the army and fled first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor abandoned the army and fled first.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，入晉陽，憂懼不知所之。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, he entered Jinyang, anxious and fearful, not knowing where to turn.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou he entered Jinyang, stricken with fear and at a loss.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin a general pardon was declared.

sentences.zh: 帝謂朝臣曰：「周師甚盛，若何？

translations.literal: The Emperor said to the court ministers: "The Zhou armies are very strong; what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the court: "The Zhou armies are very strong; what shall we do?

sentences.zh: 」群臣咸曰：「天命未改，一得一失，自古皆然。

translations.literal: " All the ministers said: "Heaven's mandate has not changed; one gain and one loss have been thus since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: " All replied: "Heaven's mandate has not changed; gain and loss have always alternated.

sentences.zh: 宜停百賦，安朝野，收遺兵，背城死戰，以存社稷。

translations.literal: All levies should be halted, the court and countryside calmed, scattered troops gathered, and a death fight fought with the city at one's back to preserve the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Stop all levies, calm court and countryside, gather the scattered troops, and fight to the death with the city at your back to save the realm.

sentences.zh: 」帝意猶預，欲向北朔州。

translations.literal: " The Emperor still hesitated and wished to flee north to Shuo Province.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor still hesitated and wished to flee north to Shuo Province.

sentences.zh: 乃留安德王廷宗、廣寧王孝珩等守晉陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he left Prince of Ande Tingzong, Prince of Guangning Xiaoxing, and others to hold Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then left Prince of Ande Tingzong and Prince of Guangning Xiaoxing to hold Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 若晉陽不守，即欲奔突厥。

translations.literal: If Jinyang could not be held, he intended to flee to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: If Jinyang fell, he meant to flee to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆曰不可，帝不從其言。

translations.literal: The ministers all said this could not be done, but the Emperor would not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all said this was impossible, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司賀拔伏恩、封輔相、慕容鐘葵等宿衛近臣三十餘人，西奔周師。

translations.literal: Bearer of Equal Honor with the Three Excellencies Heba Fu'en, Feng Fuxiang, Murong Zhongkui, and more than thirty other close attendants and bodyguards fled west to the Zhou armies.
translations.idiomatic: Bearer of Equal Honor with the Three Excellencies Heba Fu'en, Feng Fuxiang, Murong Zhongkui, and more than thirty bodyguards fled west to the Zhou armies.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔募兵，遣安德王延宗為左廣，廣寧王孝珩為右廣。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, an edict ordered recruitment of troops and dispatched Prince of Ande Yan Zong as Left Commander and Prince of Guangning Xiaoxing as Right Commander.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao an edict ordered levies and made Prince of Ande Yan Zong Left Commander and Prince of Guangning Xiaoxing Right Commander.

sentences.zh: 延宗入見帝，帝告欲向北朔州，延宗泣諫，不從。

translations.literal: Yan Zong entered to see the Emperor; the Emperor told him he wished to go north to Shuo Province; Yan Zong wept and remonstrated, but was not obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zong came before the emperor, who said he wished to go north to Shuo Province; Yan Zong wept and remonstrated in vain.

sentences.zh: 帝密遣王康德與中人齊紹等送皇太后、皇太子於北朔州。

translations.literal: The Emperor secretly sent Wang Kede and the eunuch Qi Shao and others to escort the Empress Dowager and crown prince to northern Shuo Province.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly sent Wang Kede and the eunuch Qi Shao to escort the Empress Dowager and crown prince to northern Shuo Province.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，帝幸城南軍營，勞將士，其夜欲遁，諸將不從。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, the Emperor visited the southern army camp to encourage the troops; that night he wished to flee, but the generals would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the emperor visited the southern camp to encourage the troops; that night he wished to flee, but the generals refused.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，大赦。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi a general pardon was declared.

sentences.zh: 改武平七年為隆化元年。

translations.literal: The seventh year of Wuping was changed to the first year of Longhua.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh year of Wuping was renamed the first year of Longhua.

sentences.zh: 其日，穆提婆降周。

translations.literal: That same day Mu Tipo surrendered to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Mu Tipo surrendered to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 詔除安德王延宗為相國，委以備禦，延宗流涕受命。

translations.literal: An edict removed Prince of Ande Yan Zong from office as Chancellor and entrusted him with defense; Yan Zong accepted through tears.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Prince of Ande Yan Zong chancellor in charge of defense; he accepted through tears.

sentences.zh: 帝乃夜斬五龍門而出。

translations.literal: The Emperor then cut through the Five Dragon Gate by night and went out.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor cut through the Five Dragon Gate and fled.

sentences.zh: 欲走突厥，從官多散，領軍梅勝郎叩馬諫，乃回之鄴。

translations.literal: He wished to flee to the Turks; many attendants scattered; Guard General Mei Sheng Lang seized his horse and remonstrated, and he turned back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to flee to the Turks; attendants scattered; Guard General Mei Sheng Lang seized his horse and remonstrated, and he turned back to Ye.

sentences.zh: 時唯高阿那肱等十餘騎，廣寧王孝珩、襄城王彥道續至，得數十人同行。

translations.literal: At that time only Gao Anagou and a dozen horsemen remained; Prince of Guangning Xiaoxing and Prince of Xiangcheng Yandao arrived afterward, and several dozen men went on together.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gao Anagou and a dozen riders remained; Prince of Guangning Xiaoxing and Prince of Xiangcheng Yandao joined later with several dozen men.

sentences.zh: 戊午，延宗從眾議，即皇帝位於晉陽，改隆化為德昌元年。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, Yan Zong followed the general will and took the imperial throne at Jinyang, changing Longhua to the first year of Dechang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Yan Zong, following the general will, took the throne at Jinyang and changed Longhua to Dechang year one.

sentences.zh: 庚申，帝入鄴。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen, the Emperor entered Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the emperor entered Ye.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，延宗與周師戰於晉陽，大敗，為周師所虜。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Yan Zong fought the Zhou armies at Jinyang and was utterly defeated and captured by the Zhou armies.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Yan Zong fought the Zhou at Jinyang, was routed, and was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 帝遣募人，重加官賞，雖有此言，而竟不出物。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered recruitment of men with added rank and reward, but though he said this, in the end he gave nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promised rank and reward to recruits, but in the end gave nothing.

sentences.zh: 廣寧王孝珩奏請出宮人及珍寶，班賜將士，帝不悅。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangning Xiaoxing memorialized asking that palace women and treasures be distributed to reward the troops; the Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guangning Xiaoxing asked that palace women and treasures be given to reward the troops; the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 斛律孝卿居中，受委帶甲以處分。

translations.literal: Hulu Xiaoqing held the center, entrusted with authority and wearing armor to direct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hulu Xiaoqing held the center, entrusted with authority and armored to direct affairs.

sentences.zh: 請帝親勞，為帝撰辭，且曰：「宜慷慨流涕，感激人心。

translations.literal: He asked the Emperor to appear in person to encourage the troops, drafted a speech for him, and said: "You should weep freely and move men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the emperor to appear in person to encourage the troops, drafted a speech, and said: "You should weep freely and stir men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 」帝既出臨眾，將令之，不復記所受言，遂大笑。

translations.literal: " When the Emperor came out before the host and was about to deliver the order, he no longer remembered what he had been told and burst into laughter.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor came out before the host to speak, he forgot what he had been told and burst into laughter.

sentences.zh: 左右亦群咍，將士莫不解體。

translations.literal: Those around him also roared with laughter; the officers and soldiers were utterly disheartened.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him laughed too; officers and soldiers were utterly disheartened.

sentences.zh: 於是自大丞相已下，太宰、大司馬、三師、大將軍、三公等官，並增員而授，或三或四，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Grand Chancellor downward, posts of Grand Preceptor, Grand Marshal, the Three Preceptors, Grand General, the Three Excellencies, and others were all increased in number and filled, some with three or four incumbents, beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon from Grand Chancellor downward, posts of Grand Preceptor, Grand Marshal, the Three Preceptors, Grand General, and the Three Excellencies were multiplied, some with three or four holders, beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 甲子，皇太后從北道至。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, the Empress Dowager arrived by the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the Empress Dowager arrived by the northern route.

sentences.zh: 引文武一品已上入朱華門。

translations.literal: Officials of the first rank and above in civil and military service were summoned into Zhuhua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials of first rank and above were summoned into Zhuhua Gate.

sentences.zh: 賜酒食及紙筆，問以禦周之方略。

translations.literal: Wine, food, paper, and brushes were granted, and they were asked for strategy against Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: They were given wine, food, paper, and brushes and asked for strategy against Zhou.

sentences.zh: 群臣各異議，帝莫知所從。

translations.literal: The ministers each offered different views, and the Emperor did not know whom to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Each minister offered a different view, and the emperor knew not whom to follow.

sentences.zh: 又引高元海、宋士素、盧思道、李德林等欲議禪位皇太子。

translations.literal: Gao Yuanhai, Song Shisu, Lu Sidao, and Li Delin were also summoned to discuss abdicating the throne to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuanhai, Song Shisu, Lu Sidao, and Li Delin were also summoned to discuss abdicating to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 先是，望氣者言，當有革易，於是依天統故事，授位幼主。

translations.literal: Earlier, practitioners of geomancy had said there would be a dynastic change; therefore, following the precedent of Tiantong, the throne was transferred to the Young Ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Geomancers had foretold a dynastic change; following the Tiantong precedent, the throne was transferred to the Young Ruler.

sentences.zh: 幼主名恒，帝之長子也。

translations.literal: The Young Ruler, named Heng, was the Emperor's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: The Young Ruler, named Heng, was the emperor's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 母曰穆皇后。

translations.literal: His mother was Empress Mu.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Mu.

sentences.zh: 武平元年六月，生於鄴。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Wuping, he was born at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping year one, sixth month, he was born at Ye.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month he was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: That year, tenth month, he was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 隆化二年春正月乙亥，即皇帝位，時年八歲。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the second year of Longhua, on the day yihai, he took the imperial throne; he was eight years old.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Longhua year two, first month, on yihai, he took the throne; he was eight years old.

sentences.zh: 改元為承光元年，大赦。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to the first year of Chengguang, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The reign title became Chengguang year one and a general pardon was declared.

sentences.zh: 尊皇太后為太皇太后，帝為太上皇帝，後為太上皇后。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was honored as Grand Empress Dowager, the Emperor as Retired Emperor, and the empress as Retired Empress.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was honored as Grand Empress Dowager, the emperor as Retired Emperor, and the empress as Retired Empress.

sentences.zh: 於是黃門侍郎顏之推、中書侍郎薛道衡、侍中陳德信等勸太上皇帝往河外募兵，更為經略。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yellow Gate Gentleman Yan Zhitui, Secretariat Gentleman Xue Daoheng, Palace Attendant Chen Dexin, and others urged the Retired Emperor to go beyond the river to levy troops and plan anew.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Gentleman Yan Zhitui, Secretariat Gentleman Xue Daoheng, Palace Attendant Chen Dexin, and others urged the Retired Emperor to go beyond the river to raise troops and plan anew.

sentences.zh: 若不濟，南投陳國。

translations.literal: If that did not succeed, they would flee south to the state of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: If that failed, they would flee south to Chen.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: He agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，太皇太后、太上皇自鄴先趣濟州。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, the Grand Empress Dowager and Retired Emperor left Ye first and hurried to Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the Grand Empress Dowager and Retired Emperor left Ye first and hurried toward Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 周師漸逼。

translations.literal: The Zhou armies pressed closer.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou armies closed in.

sentences.zh: 癸未，幼主又自鄴東走。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, the Young Ruler again fled east from Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei the Young Ruler fled east from Ye again.

sentences.zh: 己丑，周師至紫陽橋。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, the Zhou armies reached Ziyang Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the Zhou armies reached Ziyang Bridge.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，燒城西門，太上皇將百餘騎東走。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, the western gate was burned; the Retired Emperor fled east with a little over a hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the western gate was burned; the Retired Emperor fled east with a little over a hundred riders.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，度河入濟州。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, he crossed the river and entered Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai he crossed the river and entered Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 其日，幼主禪位於大丞相、任城王湝，令侍中斛律孝卿送禪文及璽紱於瀛州。

translations.literal: That same day the Young Ruler abdicated the throne to Grand Chancellor Prince of Rencheng Hui, and ordered Palace Attendant Hulu Xiaoqing to deliver the abdication document and imperial seal and cord to Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Young Ruler abdicated to Grand Chancellor Prince of Rencheng Hui and ordered Palace Attendant Hulu Xiaoqing to deliver the abdication text and imperial seal and cord to Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 孝卿乃以之歸周。

translations.literal: Xiaoqing then took them to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoqing then took them to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 又為任城王詔，尊太上皇為無上皇。

translations.literal: An edict was also issued in the name of Prince of Rencheng honoring the Retired Emperor as Supreme Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was also issued in Prince of Rencheng's name honoring the Retired Emperor as Supreme Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 幼主為守國天王。

translations.literal: The Young Ruler was made Heavenly King Guarding the State.
translations.idiomatic: The Young Ruler was made Heavenly King Guarding the State.

sentences.zh: 留太皇太后濟州，遣高阿那肱留守。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager was left at Ji Province, and Gao Anagou was left to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager was left at Ji Province and Gao Anagou was left to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 太上皇並皇后攜幼主走青州，韓長鸞、鄧颙等數十人從。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor, the empress, and the Young Ruler fled to Qing Province, accompanied by Han Changluan, Deng Yong, and several dozen others.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor, the empress, and the Young Ruler fled to Qing Province with Han Changluan, Deng Yong, and several dozen others.

sentences.zh: 太上皇既至青州，即為入陳之計。

translations.literal: Once the Retired Emperor reached Qing Province, he at once planned to enter Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Qing Province, the Retired Emperor at once planned to enter Chen.

sentences.zh: 而高阿那肱召周軍，約生致齊主。

translations.literal: But Gao Anagou summoned the Zhou armies and agreed to deliver the Qi ruler alive.
translations.idiomatic: But Gao Anagou summoned the Zhou armies and agreed to deliver the Qi ruler alive.

sentences.zh: 而屢使人告，言賊軍在遠，已令人燒斷橋路。

translations.literal: Yet he repeatedly sent word saying the enemy was far off and that he had already had the bridges burned and the roads cut.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he repeatedly sent word that the enemy was far off and that he had already burned the bridges and cut the roads.

sentences.zh: 太上所以停緩。

translations.literal: This was why the Retired Emperor halted and delayed.
translations.idiomatic: This was why the Retired Emperor halted and delayed.

sentences.zh: 周軍奄至青州，太上窘急，將遜於陳，置金囊於鞍後。

translations.literal: The Zhou armies suddenly reached Qing Province; the Retired Emperor was in dire straits and was about to flee to Chen; he placed a gold pouch behind his saddle.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou armies suddenly reached Qing Province; the Retired Emperor, in dire straits, was about to flee to Chen and placed a gold pouch behind his saddle.

sentences.zh: 與長鸞、淑妃等十數騎至青州南鄧村，為周將尉暹綱所獲，送鄴。

translations.literal: With Changluan, the Honored Consort, and a dozen horsemen he reached Deng Village south of Qingzhou and was captured by Zhou general Wei Xiangang and sent to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: With Changluan, the Honored Consort, and a dozen riders he reached Deng Village south of Qing Province and was captured by Zhou general Wei Xiangang and sent to Ye.

sentences.zh: 周武帝與抗賓主禮，並太后、幼主、諸王，俱送長安。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou treated him with the etiquette due a guest and host, and together with the empress dowager, the Young Ruler, and the princes, all were sent to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Emperor Wu treated him with guest-and-host etiquette and sent the empress dowager, the Young Ruler, and the princes together to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 封帝溫國公。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enfeoffed as Duke of Wen State.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enfeoffed as Duke of Wen State.

sentences.zh: 至建德七年，誣與宜州刺史穆提婆謀反，及延宗等數十人，無少長咸賜死。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiande, he was falsely accused of plotting rebellion with Governor of Yi Province Mu Tipo; he and Yan Zong and several dozen others, without distinction of age, were all granted death.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande year seven he was falsely accused of plotting rebellion with Governor of Yi Province Mu Tipo; he and Yan Zong and several dozen others, without distinction of age, were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 神武子孫所存者一二而己。

translations.literal: Of Shenwu's descendants only one or two remained.
translations.idiomatic: Of Shenwu's descendants only one or two remained.

sentences.zh: 至大象末，陽休之、陳德信等啟大丞相隋公，請收葬。

translations.literal: By the end of Daxiang, Yang Xiuzhi, Chen Dexin, and others petitioned Grand Chancellor Duke of Sui to allow burial.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Daxiang, Yang Xiuzhi, Chen Dexin, and others petitioned Grand Chancellor the Duke of Sui to allow burial.

sentences.zh: 聽之，葬於長安北原洪瀆川。

translations.literal: Permission was granted, and they were buried on the northern plain of Chang'an at Hongdu Stream.
translations.idiomatic: Permission was granted, and they were buried on the northern plain of Chang'an at Hongdu Stream.

sentences.zh: 帝幼而令善；

translations.literal: As a child the Emperor was clever and good;
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was clever and good;

sentences.zh: 及長，頗學綴文，置文林館，引諸文士焉。

translations.literal: when he grew up he studied literary composition to some degree, established the Wenlin Hall, and gathered literary men there.
translations.idiomatic: when he grew he studied composition, established the Wenlin Hall, and gathered literary men there.

sentences.zh: 而言語澀吶，無誌度，不喜見朝士。

translations.literal: Yet his speech was halting, he had no fixed purpose, and he disliked seeing court officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his speech was halting, he had no fixed purpose, and he disliked seeing court officials.

sentences.zh: 自非寵私昵狎，未嘗交語。

translations.literal: Unless they were favorites with whom he was intimate, he never exchanged words with them.
translations.idiomatic: Unless they were intimate favorites, he never spoke with them.

sentences.zh: 性懦不堪，人視者即有忿責。

translations.literal: His nature was timid and unfit for pressure; if anyone looked at him he would fly into a rage.
translations.idiomatic: He was timid and brittle; if anyone looked at him he would fly into a rage.

sentences.zh: 其奏事者，雖三公、令、錄莫得仰視。

translations.literal: Those who reported affairs, even the Three Excellencies, the Minister of Works, and the Recorder, might not look up at him.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Three Excellencies, the Minister of Works, and the Recorder might not look up when reporting affairs.

sentences.zh: 皆略陳大旨，驚走而出。

translations.literal: They would state the main points briefly and flee out in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: They would state the gist briefly and flee out in alarm.

sentences.zh: 每災異寇盜水旱，亦不自貶損；

translations.literal: Whenever there were omens, bandits, floods, or drought, he never blamed himself;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever omens, bandits, floods, or drought struck, he never blamed himself;

sentences.zh: 唯諸處設齋，以此為修德。

translations.literal: he only ordered vegetarian feasts at various places, taking this as cultivating virtue.
translations.idiomatic: he only ordered vegetarian feasts here and there, calling it cultivating virtue.

sentences.zh: 雅信巫覡，解禱無方。

translations.literal: He greatly trusted shamans and sorcerers and knew no limit to prayer and exorcism.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly trusted shamans and knew no limit to prayer and exorcism.

sentences.zh: 初，瑯邪王舉兵，人告者誤雲庫狄伏連反，帝曰：「此必仁威也。

translations.literal: At first, when Prince of Langye raised troops, an informer mistakenly said Kudi Fulian had rebelled; the Emperor said: "This must be Renwei.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Langye raised troops, an informer mistakenly said Kudi Fulian had rebelled; the emperor said: "This must be Renwei.

sentences.zh: 」又斛律光死後，諸武官舉高思好堪大將軍，帝曰：「思好喜反。

translations.literal: " After Hulu Guang died, the military officials recommended Gao Sihao as fit for Grand General; the Emperor said: "Sihao loves rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " After Hulu Guang died, military officials recommended Gao Sihao for Grand General; the emperor said: "Sihao loves rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」皆如所言，遂自以策無遺算，乃益驕縱。

translations.literal: " In each case it was as he said, and he came to believe his judgment missed nothing, growing ever more arrogant and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: " Each time he was right, and he came to believe his judgment missed nothing, growing ever more arrogant and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 盛為無愁之曲，帝自彈胡琵琶而唱之，侍和之者以百數，人間謂之無愁天子。

translations.literal: He composed at length the Song of Carefree Sorrow; the Emperor himself played the foreign pipa and sang it, and those who joined in the chorus numbered in the hundreds; people called him the Carefree Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He composed at length the Song of Carefree Sorrow, played the foreign pipa and sang it himself, with hundreds joining the chorus; people called him the Carefree Emperor.

sentences.zh: 嘗出見群厲，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Once when he went out and saw a swarm of locusts, he killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he went out and saw locusts, he killed them all.

sentences.zh: 或殺人，剝面皮而視之。

translations.literal: Sometimes when he killed a man, he flayed the face and looked at it.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes when he killed a man, he flayed the face and looked at it.

sentences.zh: 任陸令萱、和士開、高阿那肱、穆提婆、韓長鸞等宰制天下；

translations.literal: He entrusted Lu Lingxuan, He Shikai, Gao Anagou, Mu Tipo, and Han Changluan with mastery over the realm;
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted Lu Lingxuan, He Shikai, Gao Anagou, Mu Tipo, and Han Changluan with mastery over the realm;

sentences.zh: 陳德信、鄧長颙、何洪珍參預機權。

translations.literal: Chen Dexin, Deng Changyong, and He Hongzhen shared in the exercise of power.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Dexin, Deng Changyong, and He Hongzhen shared in the exercise of power.

sentences.zh: 各引親黨，超居非次；

translations.literal: Each brought in his own partisans and was promoted beyond proper rank;
translations.idiomatic: Each brought in his own partisans and was promoted beyond proper rank;

sentences.zh: 官由財進，獄以賄成；

translations.literal: office came through wealth, and prisons through bribes;
translations.idiomatic: office came through wealth and prisons through bribes;

sentences.zh: 其所以亂政害人。

translations.literal: this was how they ruined government and harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: this was how they ruined government and harmed the people.

sentences.zh: 難以備載。

translations.literal: It is hard to record it all.
translations.idiomatic: It is hard to record it all.

sentences.zh: 諸官奴婢、閹人、商人、胡戶、雜戶、歌舞人、見鬼人濫得富貴者，將以萬數。

translations.literal: Official slaves and maidservants, eunuchs, merchants, foreign households, miscellaneous households, singers and dancers, and spirit-mediums who improperly gained wealth and rank numbered nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Official slaves, eunuchs, merchants, foreign households, miscellaneous households, singers, dancers, and spirit-mediums who improperly gained wealth and rank numbered nearly ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 庶姓封王者百數，不復可紀。

translations.literal: Commoners enfeoffed as princes numbered in the hundreds, beyond further reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners enfeoffed as princes numbered in the hundreds, beyond further reckoning.

sentences.zh: 開府千餘，儀同無數。

translations.literal: Bearer of the Office numbered over a thousand; Bearer of Equal Honor was beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Bearer of the Office numbered over a thousand; Bearer of Equal Honor was beyond count.

sentences.zh: 領軍一時三十，連判文書，各作依字，不具姓名，莫知誰也。

translations.literal: At one time there were thirty Guard Generals; they countersigned documents in succession, each writing the character for "approved" without giving a full name, and no one knew who was who.
translations.idiomatic: At one time there were thirty Guard Generals; they countersigned documents in succession, each writing "approved" without a full name, and no one knew who was who.

sentences.zh: 諸貴寵祖禰追贈，官歲一進，位極乃止。

translations.literal: For all the favorites, ancestors and forefathers were posthumously enfeoffed, their offices advancing one rank each year until the highest rank was reached.
translations.idiomatic: For all favorites, ancestors were posthumously enfeoffed, their offices advancing one rank each year until the highest rank was reached.

sentences.zh: 宮掖婢皆封郡君。

translations.literal: Palace maidservants were all enfeoffed as commandery ladies.
translations.idiomatic: Palace maidservants were all enfeoffed as commandery ladies.

sentences.zh: 宮女寶衣玉食者五百餘人。

translations.literal: Palace women in jeweled robes and jade fare numbered more than five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women in jeweled robes and jade fare numbered more than five hundred.

sentences.zh: 一裙直萬疋，鏡臺直千金。

translations.literal: One skirt cost ten thousand bolts, and one mirror stand a thousand in gold.
translations.idiomatic: One skirt cost ten thousand bolts, and one mirror stand a thousand in gold.

sentences.zh: 競為變巧，朝衣夕弊。

translations.literal: They vied in novelty and artifice; robes worn in the morning were worn out by evening.
translations.idiomatic: They vied in novelty and artifice; robes worn in the morning were worn out by evening.

sentences.zh: 承武成之奢麗，以為帝王當然。

translations.literal: Following Wucheng's extravagance, he took this as what an emperor ought to be.
translations.idiomatic: Following Wucheng's extravagance, he took this as what an emperor ought to be.

sentences.zh: 乃更增益宮苑，造偃武修文臺。

translations.literal: He then further enlarged the palace parks and built the Rest Arms and Cultivate Culture Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He then further enlarged the palace parks and built the Rest Arms and Cultivate Culture Terrace.

sentences.zh: 其嬪嬙諸院中，起鏡殿、寶殿、瑇瑁殿，丹青雕刻，妙極當時。

translations.literal: In the various courts of the consorts and ladies he erected Mirror Hall, Treasure Hall, and Tortoiseshell Hall, painted and carved to the utmost wonder of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the consorts' courts he erected Mirror Hall, Treasure Hall, and Tortoiseshell Hall, painted and carved to the utmost wonder of the age.

sentences.zh: 又於晉陽起十二院，壯麗逾於鄴下。

translations.literal: He also built twelve courts at Jinyang, more splendid than those below Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He also built twelve courts at Jinyang, more splendid than those at Ye.

sentences.zh: 所愛不恒，數毀而又復。

translations.literal: What he favored did not last; he repeatedly destroyed and rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: What he favored did not last; he repeatedly destroyed and rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 夜則以火照作，寒則以湯為泥。

translations.literal: At night they worked by torchlight; in cold weather they used hot water for mortar.
translations.idiomatic: At night they worked by torchlight; in cold weather they used hot water for mortar.

sentences.zh: 百工困窮，無時休息。

translations.literal: Artisans were exhausted and had no time to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Artisans were exhausted and had no time to rest.

sentences.zh: 鑿晉陽西山為大佛像，一夜燃油萬盆，光照宮內。

translations.literal: The western mountain at Jinyang was carved into a great Buddha image; in one night ten thousand basins of oil were burned, and the light filled the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The western mountain at Jinyang was carved into a great Buddha image; in one night ten thousand basins of oil were burned and the light filled the palace.

sentences.zh: 又為胡昭儀起大慈寺，未成，改為穆皇后大寶林寺。

translations.literal: He also built Daci Temple for Honored Consort Hu; before it was finished it was changed to Empress Mu's Dabaolin Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He also built Daci Temple for Honored Consort Hu; before it was finished it was changed to Empress Mu's Dabaolin Temple.

sentences.zh: 窮極工巧，運石填泉，勞費億計，人牛死者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Craftsmanship was pushed to the extreme; stones were transported to fill springs; labor and expense ran to hundreds of millions; men and oxen who died were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Craftsmanship was pushed to the extreme; stones were transported to fill springs; labor and expense ran to hundreds of millions; men and oxen who died were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 御馬則藉以氈罽，食物有十餘種。

translations.literal: Imperial horses were spread with felt and rugs, and their food came in more than ten varieties.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial horses were spread with felt and rugs, and their food came in more than ten varieties.

sentences.zh: 將合牝牡，則設青廬，具牢饌而親觀之。

translations.literal: When they were to mate, a green pavilion was set up, full provisions prepared, and he watched in person.
translations.idiomatic: When they were to mate, a green pavilion was set up, full provisions prepared, and he watched in person.

sentences.zh: 狗則飼以梁肉。

translations.literal: Dogs were fed on fine grain and meat.
translations.idiomatic: Dogs were fed on fine grain and meat.

sentences.zh: 馬及鷹犬，乃有儀同、郡君之號。

translations.literal: Horses, hawks, and dogs were given titles of Bearer of Equal Honor and commandery lady.
translations.idiomatic: Horses, hawks, and dogs were given titles of Bearer of Equal Honor and commandery lady.

sentences.zh: 故有赤彪儀同、逍遙郡君、陵霄郡君。

translations.literal: Hence there were Bearer of Equal Honor Red Tiger, Commandery Lady Xiaoyao, and Commandery Lady Lingxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Hence there were Bearer of Equal Honor Red Tiger, Commandery Lady Xiaoyao, and Commandery Lady Lingxiao.

sentences.zh: 高思好書所謂馱龍，逍遙著也。

translations.literal: The "pack-dragon" in Gao Sihao's letter was Xiaoyao.
translations.idiomatic: The "pack-dragon" in Gao Sihao's letter was Xiaoyao.

sentences.zh: 犬於馬上設褥以抱之。

translations.literal: Dogs were given cushions on horseback and carried in the arms.
translations.idiomatic: Dogs were given cushions on horseback and carried in the arms.

sentences.zh: 鬥雞亦號開府。

translations.literal: Fighting cocks were also titled Bearer of the Office.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting cocks were also titled Bearer of the Office.

sentences.zh: 犬馬雞鷹，多食縣幹。

translations.literal: Dogs, horses, cocks, and hawks ate much dried meat from the counties.
translations.idiomatic: Dogs, horses, cocks, and hawks ate much dried meat from the counties.

sentences.zh: 鷹之入養者，稍割犬肉以飼之，至數日乃死。

translations.literal: Hawks being trained were fed by gradually cutting dog flesh until after several days the dog died.
translations.idiomatic: Hawks being trained were fed by gradually cutting dog flesh until after several days the dog died.

sentences.zh: 又於華林園立貧窮村舍，帝自弊衣為乞食兒。

translations.literal: He also built poor village dwellings in Hualin Garden and himself wore ragged clothes as a begging child.
translations.idiomatic: He also built poor village dwellings in Hualin Garden and himself wore ragged clothes as a begging child.

sentences.zh: 又為窮兒之市，躬自交易。

translations.literal: He also made a poor children's market and traded in person.
translations.idiomatic: He also made a poor children's market and traded in person.

sentences.zh: 寫築西鄙諸城，黑衣為羌兵；

translations.literal: He copied and built the western frontier cities, dressed men in black as Qiang soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: He copied and built the western frontier cities and dressed men in black as Qiang soldiers;

sentences.zh: 鼓噪陵之，親率內參臨拒，或實彎弓射人。

translations.literal: drums and shouts assaulted them; he personally led inner attendants to resist, and sometimes actually bent the bow and shot at men.
translations.idiomatic: drums and shouts assaulted them; he personally led inner attendants to resist, and sometimes actually bent the bow and shot at men.

sentences.zh: 自晉陽東巡，單馬馳騖，衣解發散而歸。

translations.literal: On an eastern tour from Jinyang he galloped alone; his clothes came loose and his hair fell loose as he returned.
translations.idiomatic: On an eastern tour from Jinyang he galloped alone; his clothes came loose and his hair fell loose as he returned.

sentences.zh: 又好不急之務，曾一夜索蠍，及旦，得三升。

translations.literal: He also loved useless tasks; once he demanded scorpions overnight, and by dawn three sheng had been gathered.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved useless tasks; once he demanded scorpions overnight, and by dawn three sheng had been gathered.

sentences.zh: 特愛非時之物，取求火急，皆須朝征夕辦。

translations.literal: He especially loved out-of-season things; demands were urgent and all had to be procured by evening if ordered in the morning.
translations.idiomatic: He especially loved out-of-season things; demands were urgent and all had to be procured by evening if ordered in the morning.

sentences.zh: 當勢者因之，貸一而責十焉。

translations.literal: Those in power took advantage of this, lending one and exacting ten.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power took advantage of this, lending one and exacting ten.

sentences.zh: 賦斂日重，徭役日煩；

translations.literal: Taxes grew heavier day by day, and corvée more burdensome day by day;
translations.idiomatic: Taxes grew heavier day by day, and corvée more burdensome day by day;

sentences.zh: 人力既殫，帑藏空竭。

translations.literal: human strength was exhausted and the treasury emptied.
translations.idiomatic: human strength was exhausted and the treasury emptied.

sentences.zh: 乃賜諸佞幸賣官，或得郡兩三，或得縣六七，各分州郡，下逮鄉官，亦多降中者。

translations.literal: Thereupon favorites were granted the sale of offices; some received two or three commanderies, others six or seven counties; they divided provinces and commanderies among themselves, down to village officials, many of whom were also sold.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon favorites were granted the sale of offices; some received two or three commanderies, others six or seven counties; they divided provinces and commanderies among themselves, down to village officials, many of whom were also sold.

sentences.zh: 故有敕用州主簿，敕用郡功曹。

translations.literal: Hence there were edict appointments as provincial chief clerk and edict appointments as commandery merit officer.
translations.idiomatic: Hence there were edict appointments as provincial chief clerk and edict appointments as commandery merit officer.

sentences.zh: 於是州縣職司，多出富商大賈。

translations.literal: Thereupon provincial and county functionaries mostly came from great merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon provincial and county functionaries mostly came from great merchants.

sentences.zh: 競為貪縱，人不聊生。

translations.literal: They vied in greed and excess; the people could not live.
translations.idiomatic: They vied in greed and excess; the people could not live.

sentences.zh: 爰自鄴都及諸州郡，所在征稅，百端俱起。

translations.literal: From the capital at Ye and the various provinces and commanderies, levies arose everywhere in a hundred forms.
translations.idiomatic: From Ye and the various provinces and commanderies, levies arose everywhere in a hundred forms.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸役皆漸於武成，至帝而增廣焉。

translations.literal: All these burdens had gradually begun under Wucheng and were expanded under this Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: All these burdens had gradually begun under Wucheng and were expanded under this emperor.

sentences.zh: 然未嘗有有帷薄淫穢，唯此事頗優於武成云。

translations.literal: Yet he never had the licentiousness of the inner quarters; in this alone he was somewhat better than Wucheng, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he never had the licentiousness of the inner quarters; in this alone he was somewhat better than Wucheng, it is said.

sentences.zh: 初，河清末，武成夢大猬攻破鄴城，故索境內猬膏以絕之。

translations.literal: At first, near the end of Heqing, Wucheng dreamed that a great hedgehog broke through Ye city; therefore he demanded hedgehog fat throughout the realm to exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Heqing, Wucheng dreamed that a great hedgehog broke through Ye city; therefore he demanded hedgehog fat throughout the realm to exterminate them.

sentences.zh: 識者以後主名聲與猬相協，亡齊征也。

translations.literal: The knowing said the Later Ruler's name and reputation harmonized with hedgehog, a sign of Qi's destruction.
translations.idiomatic: The knowing said the Later Ruler's name and reputation harmonized with hedgehog, a sign of Qi's destruction.

sentences.zh: 又婦人皆剪剔以著假髻；

translations.literal: Also, women all cut and shaved their hair to wear false topknots;
translations.idiomatic: Also, women all cut and shaved their hair to wear false topknots;

sentences.zh: 而危邪之，狀如飛鳥，至於南面，則髻心正西。

translations.literal: and they shaped them perilously, like flying birds; when facing south, the heart of the topknot pointed due west.
translations.idiomatic: They styled them daringly, like birds in flight; when a woman faced south, the crown of the false topknot pointed west.

sentences.zh: 始自宮內為之。

translations.literal: It began within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The fashion began in the palace.

sentences.zh: 被於四遠。

translations.literal: It spread to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: From there it spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 天意若曰：「元首翦落，危側，當走西也。」

translations.literal: Heaven's intent seemed to say: "The sovereign's hair is cut away, perilously tilted; he ought to flee west."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven seemed to say: "The ruler's hair is shorn, his position perilous and askew; he is bound to flee west."

sentences.zh: 又為刀子者，刃皆狹細，名曰盡勢。

translations.literal: Also, those who made knives had blades all narrow and fine, called "exhausted momentum."
translations.idiomatic: Knife-makers too shaped blades narrow and fine, naming them "spent force."

sentences.zh: 遊童戲者，好以兩手持繩，拂地而卻上跳，且唱曰「高末」。

translations.literal: Children at play liked to take a rope in both hands, sweep the ground, and leap upward while singing "gaomo."
translations.idiomatic: Children at play would take a rope in both hands, sweep the ground, leap upward, and sing "gaomo."

sentences.zh: 高末之言，蓋高氏運祚之末也。

translations.literal: The words "gaomo" meant the end of the Gao house's fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The words "gaomo" meant the end of the Gao clan's fortune.

sentences.zh: 然則亂亡之數，蓋有兆云。

translations.literal: Thus the signs of disorder and destruction had their portents.
translations.idiomatic: So the omens of chaos and ruin were already at hand.

sentences.zh: 論曰：武成風度高爽，經算弘長。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Wucheng's bearing was lofty and bright, his plans broad and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Wucheng carried himself with lofty clarity and planned on a broad scale.

sentences.zh: 文武之官，俱盡謀力，有帝王之量矣。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials all exhausted their counsel and strength; he had the measure of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military men gave him their full counsel and effort; he had the stature of a true emperor.

sentences.zh: 但愛狎庸豎，委以朝權；

translations.literal: But he loved and was intimate with base attendants and entrusted them with court power;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he doted on low attendants and handed them the reins of government;

sentences.zh: 帷薄之間，淫侈過度。

translations.literal: within the inner quarters, extravagance and excess went too far.
translations.idiomatic: within the inner quarters his extravagance knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 滅亡之兆，其在斯乎。

translations.literal: The portent of destruction lay in this, did it not.
translations.idiomatic: The seed of ruin lay here, did it not.

sentences.zh: 玄象告變，傳位元子；

translations.literal: The celestial signs announced change, and he transferred the throne to his son;
translations.idiomatic: When the heavens signaled change, he abdicated in favor of his son;

sentences.zh: 名號雖殊，政猶己出；

translations.literal: though the titles differed, government still came from himself;
translations.idiomatic: though titles changed, power still flowed from him;

sentences.zh: 跡有虛飾，事非憲典；

translations.literal: the act had a veneer of show, and the matter was not according to statute;
translations.idiomatic: the gesture was hollow, and the deed violated proper law;

sentences.zh: 聰明臨下，何易可誣。

translations.literal: with clear intelligence over his subjects, how could such things easily be deceived.
translations.idiomatic: with a clear-eyed court beneath him, how could such pretense long deceive anyone.

sentences.zh: 又河南、河間、樂陵等諸王，或以時嫌，或以猜忌，皆無罪而殞。

translations.literal: Also the princes of Henan, Hejian, Leling, and others were killed without crime, some because of the times' suspicions, some because of distrust.
translations.idiomatic: Princes of Henan, Hejian, Leling, and others were killed though guilty of nothing, some from suspicion of the times, some from distrust.

sentences.zh: 非所謂知命任天體大道之義也。

translations.literal: This was not what is called knowing fate, accepting Heaven, and embodying the great Way.
translations.idiomatic: This was not the conduct of one who knows fate, accepts Heaven, and embodies the great Way.

sentences.zh: 後主以中庸之姿，懷易染之性。

translations.literal: The Later Ruler, with a mediocre nature, possessed a character easily stained.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Ruler was mediocre by nature and easily corrupted.

sentences.zh: 永言先訓，教匪義方。

translations.literal: Forever speaking of his forefathers' instruction, his teaching was not the righteous way.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke always of his forefathers' instruction, yet what he received was not the righteous way.

sentences.zh: 始自繈褓，至於傳位，隔以正人，閉其善道。

translations.literal: From swaddling clothes to succession, upright men were kept apart and the good path closed to him.
translations.idiomatic: From infancy to enthronement, upright men were kept from him and the good path barred.

sentences.zh: 養德所履，異乎春誦夏弦。

translations.literal: What he tread in cultivating virtue differed from spring recitation and summer lute strings.
translations.idiomatic: The moral ground he walked was nothing like the spring recitations and summer lute lessons of old.

sentences.zh: 過廷所聞，莫非不軌不物。

translations.literal: What he heard in passing the court differed entirely from what was not proper and not right.
translations.idiomatic: What reached him at court was nothing but the improper and the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 輔之以中官奶媼，屬之以麗色淫聲；

translations.literal: He was assisted by eunuchs and wet nurses, and entrusted to beautiful women and sensual music;
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs and wet nurses raised him; beautiful women and sensual music held him;

sentences.zh: 縱巘紲之娛，恣朋淫之好。

translations.literal: he indulged the pleasure of hunting and gave free rein to debauched company.
translations.idiomatic: he indulged hunting and gave free rein to debauched companions.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「從惡若崩」，蓋言其易。

translations.literal: The saying goes: "Following evil is like an avalanche," meaning how easy it is.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, "Following evil is like an avalanche" — how swift the fall.

sentences.zh: 武平在禦，彌見淪胥；

translations.literal: During Wuping on the throne, he sank further into ruin;
translations.idiomatic: Once Wuping began, he sank deeper into ruin;

sentences.zh: 罕接朝士，不親政事；

translations.literal: he rarely received court officials and did not personally handle government;
translations.idiomatic: he rarely saw court officials and never handled affairs himself;

sentences.zh: 一日萬機，委諸凶族。

translations.literal: the myriad affairs of a day were entrusted to a vicious clan.
translations.idiomatic: the day's myriad affairs were left to a vicious clan.

sentences.zh: 內侍帷幄，外吐絲綸；

translations.literal: Within, they attended the imperial curtains; without, they issued silk edicts;
translations.idiomatic: Within the curtains they ruled; without they issued edicts;

sentences.zh: 威厲風霜，誌回天日；

translations.literal: their authority was like frost and wind, their will turning back sun and sky;
translations.idiomatic: their power was frost and wind, their will bending sun and sky;

sentences.zh: 虐人害物，搏噬無厭；

translations.literal: they harmed men and things, devouring without satiety;
translations.idiomatic: they devoured men and goods without end;

sentences.zh: 賣獄鬻官，溪壑難滿。

translations.literal: they sold prisons and offices, and ravines and gullies could not be filled.
translations.idiomatic: they sold prisons and offices, and no ravine could hold their greed.

sentences.zh: 重以名將貽禍，忠臣顯戮；

translations.literal: Added to this, famous generals brought disaster and loyal ministers were openly executed;
translations.idiomatic: Famous generals were destroyed and loyal ministers openly executed;

sentences.zh: 始見浸溺之萌，俄觀土崩之勢。

translations.literal: one first saw the sprouting of inundation, then suddenly witnessed the momentum of collapse.
translations.idiomatic: first came the first signs of flood, then suddenly the rush of collapse.

sentences.zh: 周武因機，遂混區夏，悲天！

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou seized the opportunity and unified the realm; Heaven is pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Emperor Wu seized the moment and unified the realm — Heaven have mercy!

sentences.zh: 蓋桀紂罪人，其亡也忽焉，自然之理矣。

translations.literal: Jie and Zhou were criminals against Heaven; their destruction came suddenly — such is the natural order.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Zhou were Heaven's outcasts; their fall came in a breath — such is nature's way.

sentences.zh: 鄭文貞公魏征總而論之曰：神武以雄傑之姿，始基霸業；

translations.literal: Duke Wen Zhen of Zheng, Wei Zheng, summing up and discussing it, said: Shenwu, with a heroic stature, first laid the foundation of hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen Zhen of Zheng, Wei Zheng, summed it up thus: Shenwu, heroic in stature, first laid the hegemonic foundation;

sentences.zh: 文襄以英明之略，伐叛柔遠。

translations.literal: Wenxiang, with brilliant strategy, suppressed rebels and pacified the distant.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang, brilliant in strategy, crushed rebels and pacified the frontier.

sentences.zh: 於時喪君有君，師出以律。

translations.literal: At that time when the ruler died there was still a ruler, and armies marched according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In those days when a ruler died, another stood ready, and armies marched by rule.

sentences.zh: 河陰之役，摧宇文如反掌；

translations.literal: At the Battle of Heyin, Yuwen was crushed as easily as turning the hand;
translations.idiomatic: At Heyin, Yuwen was broken as easily as turning the hand;

sentences.zh: 渦陽之戰，掃侯景如拉枯。

translations.literal: at the Battle of Woyang, Hou Jing was swept away as easily as pulling dry wood.
translations.idiomatic: at Woyang, Hou Jing was swept aside like dry wood pulled apart.

sentences.zh: 故能氣懾西鄰，威加南服。

translations.literal: Thus their spirit awed the western neighbor and their might extended to the southern domains.
translations.idiomatic: Their spirit awed the west and their might reached the southern realms.

sentences.zh: 王室是賴，東夏宅心。

translations.literal: The royal house relied on them, and the eastern lands set their hearts on them.
translations.idiomatic: The royal house leaned on them, and the eastern lands gave them their hearts.

sentences.zh: 文宣因累世之資，膺樂推之會，地居當璧，遂遷魏鼎。

translations.literal: Wenxuan, relying on the assets of successive generations and the fortune of the people's acclaim, occupied the position of the jade disk and moved the Wei tripod.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan, drawing on generations of strength and the people's acclaim, took the jade disk's place and moved the Wei tripod.

sentences.zh: 懷譎詭非常之才，運屈奇不測之智；

translations.literal: He possessed talent for devious and extraordinary schemes and employed unfathomable stratagems;
translations.idiomatic: He had a gift for devious, unfathomable schemes;

sentences.zh: 網羅俊乂，明察臨下；

translations.literal: he gathered worthy men and discerned clearly over his subjects;
translations.idiomatic: he gathered the worthy and judged his subjects with clear eyes;

sentences.zh: 文武名臣，盡其力用。

translations.literal: civil and military famous ministers all exerted their strength.
translations.idiomatic: and civil and military ministers gave all their strength.

sentences.zh: 親戎出塞，命將臨江。

translations.literal: He personally led armies beyond the frontier and dispatched generals to the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: He led armies beyond the frontier himself and sent generals to the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 定單于於龍城，納長君於梁國。

translations.literal: He settled the Xiongnu at Long City and installed the elder lord in the Liang state.
translations.idiomatic: He settled the Xiongnu at Long City and set the Liang ruler in place.

sentences.zh: 外內充實，疆場無警；

translations.literal: Within and without were full, and the borders were without alarm;
translations.idiomatic: Within and without were full, and the borders knew no alarm;

sentences.zh: 胡騎息其南侵，秦人不敢東顧。

translations.literal: Hu horsemen ceased their southern raids, and the Qin people did not dare look east.
translations.idiomatic: northern horsemen ceased their southern raids, and Qin did not dare look east.

sentences.zh: 既而荒淫敗德，罔念作狂；

translations.literal: Then he abandoned virtue in debauchery and forgot to reflect in madness;
translations.idiomatic: Then he cast virtue aside for debauchery and forgot himself in madness;

sentences.zh: 為善未能亡身，余殃足以傳後。

translations.literal: doing good could not save his person, yet residual calamity was enough to pass to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: virtue could not save him, yet the aftershock was enough to ruin his heirs.

sentences.zh: 得以壽終，幸也；

translations.literal: That he was able to die a natural death was good fortune;
translations.idiomatic: That he died in his bed was luck;

sentences.zh: 胤嗣不永，宜哉。

translations.literal: that his heirs did not long endure was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: that his line did not endure was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 孝昭地逼身危，逆取順守；

translations.literal: Xiaozhao, pressed by circumstance and in peril of body, took by rebellion and kept by compliance;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhao, pressed by circumstance and peril, seized power by force yet ruled by restraint;

sentences.zh: 外敷文教，內蘊雄圖；

translations.literal: without he spread civil teaching, within he harbored heroic designs;
translations.idiomatic: outwardly he spread civil teaching, inwardly he nursed heroic designs;

sentences.zh: 將以牢籠區域，奄有函夏。

translations.literal: he meant to envelop the realm and possess all within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: he meant to envelop the realm and hold all within the passes.

sentences.zh: 享齡不永，績用無成。

translations.literal: His years of life were not long, and his achievement was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: His years were short and his work unfinished.

sentences.zh: 若或天假之年，足使秦、吳旰食。

translations.literal: Had Heaven granted more years, he would have been enough to make Qin and Wu dine late in anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Had Heaven granted him longer life, Qin and Wu would have dined late in fear.

sentences.zh: 武成即位，雅道陵遲。

translations.literal: When Wucheng took the throne, the refined Way declined.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wucheng the refined Way declined.

sentences.zh: 昭、襄之風，摧焉已墜。

translations.literal: The wind of Zhao and Xiang was already fallen and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit of Zhao and Xiang was already fallen.

sentences.zh: 暨乎後主，外內崩離；

translations.literal: By the time of the Later Ruler, inner and outer were in collapse;
translations.idiomatic: By the Later Ruler's time, inner and outer were collapsing;

sentences.zh: 眾潰於平陽，身禽於青土。

translations.literal: the host fled at Pingyang, and the person was captured on the blue earth.
translations.idiomatic: the army broke at Pingyang, and the man was taken on the blue plain.

sentences.zh: 天道深遠，或未易談；

translations.literal: Heaven's Way is deep and far, and perhaps not easy to discuss;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's Way is deep and perhaps beyond easy speech;

sentences.zh: 吉凶由人，抑可揚榷。

translations.literal: fortune and calamity depend on men, yet can still be weighed and assessed.
translations.idiomatic: yet fortune and ruin still turn on men and can be weighed.

sentences.zh: 觀夫有齊全盛，控帶遐阻：西包汾、晉，南極江、淮，東盡海隅，北漸沙漠。

translations.literal: Observing Qi in its full flourishing, it controlled distant barriers: west enclosing Fen and Jin, south reaching the Yangtze and Huai, east extending to the sea's edge, north encroaching on the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Qi at its height held the far barriers: Fen and Jin to the west, the Yangtze and Huai to the south, the sea to the east, the desert to the north.

sentences.zh: 六國之地，我獲其五；

translations.literal: Of the Six States' lands, we held five;
translations.idiomatic: Of the Six States' lands, Qi held five;

sentences.zh: 九州之境，彼分其四。

translations.literal: of the Nine Provinces' territories, they held four.
translations.idiomatic: of the Nine Provinces, Zhou held four.

sentences.zh: 料甲兵之眾寡，校帑藏之虛實；

translations.literal: Estimating the multitude of armor and troops, comparing the emptiness and fullness of the treasury;
translations.idiomatic: Count armor and troops, weigh treasury full against empty;

sentences.zh: 折沖千里之將，帷幄六奇之士，比二方之優劣，無等級以寄言。

translations.literal: generals who could break the enemy a thousand li away, strategists of the six stratagems in the command tent — comparing the superiority and inferiority of the two sides, there was no rank by which to speak.
translations.idiomatic: generals who broke the enemy a thousand li off, strategists of the six arts in the tent — between the two sides there was no clear rank of strength.

sentences.zh: 然其太行、長城之固，自若也；

translations.literal: Yet the solidity of the Taihang and Great Wall remained as before;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Taihang and the Great Wall stood as firm as ever;

sentences.zh: 江、淮、汾、晉之險，不移也；

translations.literal: the peril of the Yangtze, Huai, Fen, and Jin did not shift;
translations.idiomatic: the Yangtze, Huai, Fen, and Jin remained as perilous;

sentences.zh: 帑藏輸稅之富，未虧也；

translations.literal: the wealth of the treasury and transport taxes was not diminished;
translations.idiomatic: treasury wealth and transport taxes were not yet spent;

sentences.zh: 士庶甲兵之眾，不缺也。

translations.literal: the multitude of gentry, commoners, armor, and troops was not lacking.
