translations.idiomatic: gentry, commoners, armor, and troops were not yet wanting.

sentences.zh: 然而前王用之而有餘，後主守之而不足，其故何哉？

translations.literal: Yet the former kings used it and had surplus, while the Later Ruler guarded it and had not enough — why was this?
translations.idiomatic: Yet earlier kings used these assets and had surplus, while the Later Ruler guarded them and still fell short — why?

sentences.zh: 前王之御時也，沐雨櫛風；

translations.literal: When the former kings ruled the age, they were drenched by rain and combed by wind;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier kings ruled drenched by rain and combed by wind;

sentences.zh: 拯其溺而救其焚，信必賞，過必罰，安而利之。

translations.literal: they rescued the drowning and saved the burning; trust was surely rewarded and faults surely punished; they secured and benefited the people.
translations.idiomatic: they rescued the drowning and the burning; merit was rewarded and fault punished; they secured and benefited the people.

sentences.zh: 既與共其存亡，故得同其生死。

translations.literal: Having shared survival and destruction with them, they therefore shared life and death with them.
translations.idiomatic: Having shared survival and ruin with the people, they shared life and death with them.

sentences.zh: 後主則不然。

translations.literal: The Later Ruler was not so.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Ruler did none of this.

sentences.zh: 以人從欲，損物益己。

translations.literal: He used men to follow his desires and harmed things to benefit himself.
translations.idiomatic: He used men to serve his desires and harmed the realm to enrich himself.

sentences.zh: 雕墻峻宇，甘酒嗜音；

translations.literal: Carved walls and towering houses, sweet wine and fondness for music;
translations.idiomatic: Carved walls and towering halls, sweet wine and endless music;

sentences.zh: 廛肆遍於宮園，禽色荒於外內。

translations.literal: market stalls filled the palace gardens, and birds and women ran wild within and without.
translations.idiomatic: markets filled the palace gardens, and birds and women ran wild inside and out.

sentences.zh: 俾晝作夜，罔水行舟；

translations.literal: He made day into night and sailed boats on dry land;
translations.idiomatic: He turned day into night and sailed boats on dry ground;

sentences.zh: 所欲必成，所求必得。

translations.literal: what he wished was surely accomplished, and what he sought was surely obtained.
translations.idiomatic: what he wished came to pass, and what he sought was his.

sentences.zh: 既不軌不物，又暗於聽受；

translations.literal: Neither proper nor fitting in conduct, he was also dark in listening;
translations.idiomatic: Improper in conduct and deaf in judgment;

sentences.zh: 忠信弗聞，萋斐必入。

translations.literal: loyalty and trust were not heard, and slander was sure to enter.
translations.idiomatic: loyalty went unheard while slander always entered.

sentences.zh: 視人如草芥，從惡如順流。

translations.literal: He viewed men like grass and followed evil like a downstream current.
translations.idiomatic: He treated men like grass and followed evil like a downstream current.

sentences.zh: 佞閹處當軸之權，婢媼擅回天之力。

translations.literal: Flatterers and eunuchs held the power of the axle; wet nurses and maidservants wielded the strength to turn back Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Flatterers and eunuchs held the axle's power; wet nurses and maidservants bent Heaven back to their will.

sentences.zh: 賣官鬻獄，亂政淫刑；

translations.literal: They sold offices and prisons, ruined government and debauched punishments;
translations.idiomatic: They sold offices and prisons, ruined government and debauched justice;

sentences.zh: 刳剒被於忠良，祿位加於犬馬。

translations.literal: mutilation fell on the loyal and good, and rank and stipend were added to dogs and horses.
translations.idiomatic: the loyal were mutilated while dogs and horses received rank and stipend.

sentences.zh: 讒邪並進，法令多聞。

translations.literal: Slander and evil advanced together, and laws and orders were many in name.
translations.idiomatic: Slander and evil rose together, and laws multiplied in name only.

sentences.zh: 持瓢者非止百人，搖樹者不唯一手。

translations.literal: Those holding ladles were not merely a hundred; those shaking the tree were not merely one hand.
translations.idiomatic: Those dipping the ladle were more than a hundred; those shaking the tree were more than one hand.

sentences.zh: 於是土崩瓦解，眾叛親離。

translations.literal: Then the earth collapsed and tiles crumbled; the host rebelled and kin deserted.
translations.idiomatic: Then earth and tile collapsed together; armies rebelled and kin deserted.

sentences.zh: 顧瞻周道，咸有西歸之志。

translations.literal: Looking back at the Zhou Way, all had the will to turn west.
translations.idiomatic: Looking toward the Zhou Way, all wished to turn west.

sentences.zh: 方更盛其宮觀，窮極荒淫；

translations.literal: Yet he further enlarged his palaces and halls and pursued extravagance to the extreme;
translations.idiomatic: Yet he enlarged his palaces further and pursued extravagance to the limit;

sentences.zh: 謂黔首之可誣，指白日以自保。

translations.literal: he thought the common people could be deceived and pointed to the bright sun to preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: he thought the people could be fooled and pointed to the bright sun to save himself.

sentences.zh: 驅倒戈之旅，抗前歌之師；

translations.literal: He drove troops who had turned their spears and resisted armies singing before them;
translations.idiomatic: He drove men who had turned their spears against him and faced armies singing in advance;

sentences.zh: 五世崇基，一舉而滅。

translations.literal: The foundation glorified through five generations was destroyed in one move.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations of glory were undone in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 豈非鐫金石者難為功，摧枯朽者易為力歟。

translations.literal: Was it not because carving stone is hard to accomplish, while crushing dry rot is easy?
translations.idiomatic: Was it not because stone is hard to carve, but dry rot easy to crush?

sentences.zh: 抑又聞之，「皇天無親，唯德是輔」。

translations.literal: It is also heard that "High Heaven is without partiality; only virtue is its aid."
translations.idiomatic: It is also said: "High Heaven shows no favoritism; only virtue wins its support."

sentences.zh: 「天時不如地利，地利不如人和」。

translations.literal: "Heaven's timing is not as good as earth's advantage; earth's advantage is not as good as human harmony."
translations.idiomatic: "Heaven's timing is less than earth's advantage; earth's advantage is less than human harmony."

sentences.zh: 齊自河清之後，逮於武平之末，土木之工不息，嬪嬙之選無已。

translations.literal: From after Heqing until the end of Wuping, construction in earth and wood never ceased, and selection of consorts and ladies never stopped.
translations.idiomatic: From after Heqing through the end of Wuping, building never stopped and the search for consorts and ladies never ended.

sentences.zh: 征稅盡，人力殫，物產無以給其求，江海不能贍其欲。

translations.literal: Levies were exhausted, human strength spent, and produce could not meet the demand; seas and rivers could not satisfy the desire.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were drained dry, labor exhausted, and the land could not feed the appetite; seas and rivers could not fill the want.

sentences.zh: 所謂火既熾矣，更負薪以足之；

translations.literal: This is what is called: the fire was already blazing, yet more fuel was piled on to fill it;
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by: the fire was already blazing, yet more fuel was piled on;

sentences.zh: 數既窮矣，又為惡以促之。

translations.literal: the count was already at its end, yet more evil was done to hasten it.
translations.idiomatic: the tally was already spent, yet more evil was done to hurry the end.

sentences.zh: 欲求大廈不燔，延期過歷，不亦難乎。

translations.literal: To wish that the great house not burn, and to prolong the years of the dynasty — would that not be difficult?
translations.idiomatic: To hope the great house would not burn and the dynasty endure — how could that have been easy?

sentences.zh: 由此言之，齊氏之敗亡，蓋亦由人，匪惟天道也。

translations.literal: From this it is said: the destruction of the Qi house was also due to men, and not only to Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: From this we may say: Qi's fall came from men as well, and not from Heaven alone.
